newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas continues to rise on keen buying, high SAP.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas continues to rise on keen buying, high SAP.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw prices continue to firm across all periods on Monday, traders and brokers said, with the fourth quarter of this year posting the steepest rises of the day.

A trader said there were three main reasons for the continuing strength in the market. First, the SAP (system average price, at which the flexibility mechanism buys and sells gas) is high; second, there is "consistent buying by certain parties"; and third, there is "a lack of offered gas."
Another dealer added that the first quarter next year had come up steeply in the last four days, and said Monday's rises showed the rest of the forward curve catching up.
Some players still anticipate a retracement following the rise.
"I guess we're just about due a correction at some stage," said a trader, although he added he thought prices may continue to rise by up to another 0.75 pence a therm.
Some believed that traders will soon start looking for profit-taking opportunities by selling on some of their recently-acquired gas.

Short term activity was comparatively muted, with no flexibility mechanism trade seen over the weekend. But the third quarter, the nearest period to see active trade, moved up over the day, with 11.20 pence done early and 11.65 pence done later in the afternoon, with trade seen at 11.45 pence in between.

Q4 was also traded in a wide range, between 14.20 pence and 14.40 pence a therm. It was reported bid at 14.60 pence a therm by the close. This followed a buy/sell range on Friday evening of 13.80/14.10 pence a therm.
The first quarter was rumoured done at 17.30 pence a therm, although this could not be confirmed.

One trader said he thought the quarter was up by 0.20 pence from Friday, much less than other periods and consistent with the theory that the main price movements were in other quarters catching up with Q1.
Summer 1998 also closed higher, and there was good volume of trade in the October gas year at both the NBP and St Fergus, done significantly higher than on Friday.

While the OTC market was trading busily, the IPE suffered its first completely blank day, with no trade done at all. By the close there was not a single offer posted, and bids were few and far between.

Transco announced a demand forecast for Tuesday of 203 mcm, or 47 percent of peak day demand, with the temperature forecast at 11.3 Celsius, higher than Monday's 10.7 Celsius but still below the seasonal normal 12.6 Celsius.
